notes.problem: Board and authored primitive review only. No render or listening verdict is claimed. The premise and mineral art differ materially from September 15th water networks and September 14th paper highway. The patterned core is a useful throughline and the first physical descent pays off by 0.82s. However, several named attention events are only label, arrow or opacity changes in provingground.tsx, so a mechanical pass does not establish the claimed action cadence.
notes.fix: Preserve the new mineral premise. Implement the specific subject changes below before the animatic, then inspect with annotations hidden. Treat camera motion and decorative traces as supporting motion only.

notes.problem: reveal-engineered promises an inset exposing mineral inclusions. In well mode, b only fades an ENGINEERED/MINERAL ROCK label and leader line; no new material or inset is revealed. The core is also small relative to the surrounding cutaway.
notes.fix: Open a large literal cut-face inset showing the same inclusion pattern, connected to the descending core; make the reveal itself the action. Keep the proposed/schematic qualification visible. Do not count the annotation fade as an attention beat.

notes.problem: The mould is a specific manufacturing method not stated by the supplied claims, and the rock is drawn on top of the closed halves. This risks showing an asserted process rather than an honest conceptual illustration. The story also jumps back to fabrication after two shots showing the specimen already downhole.
notes.fix: Mark this as a conceptual view of engineered material, not a sourced fabrication method. Either use an abstract assembly jig or retain a visibly schematic mould with proper occlusion. Motivate the temporal return through a match on the same distinctive core and make its move into the casing a continuous visible action.

notes.problem: repeat-trial only fades a circular arrow and REPEAT TEST text. That is an animated graphic, not another trial or changed subject. The sensor trace is also drawn as a measured-looking zigzag; the primitive does not itself carry its required illustration limit.
notes.fix: Have the bit retract from a persistently cut specimen and a real tray or replacement apparatus begin the next trial. Keep the core damaged. Mark the trace schematic where it is visible, and let the readout develop in response to contact rather than claiming that a decorative path alone demonstrates a result.

notes.problem: The promised oilfield tool transfer is not literal. The left drill only moves to x200 while a second drill already occupies x645. An arrow supplies the relationship. close-control moves the two collar coordinates farther apart, which opens them despite the board saying close.
notes.fix: Follow one recognizable tool from its left mount into the mineral station, then show the control apparatus physically engage it. Reverse the collar directions and connect their engagement to the tool movement. The transfer should remain understandable with OILFIELD and MINING TESTS hidden.

notes.problem: The board promises a hand reaching for a training control, but the primitive switches Character pose at a threshold while the joystick moves separately. A separately moving lever under a pointing figure may not communicate the learner causing the simulated drill response.
notes.fix: Stage a visible hand-to-control contact, then delay the wireframe drill response until the control action completes. Keep planned training explicit. Preserve the distinction between simulation and hands-on props; the film must not imply that sensor data trained a model.

notes.problem: This is the weakest stretch. read-status lifts text that is already fully exposed; hold-facility fades a bar rather than closes a barrier; open-results adds a NOT REPORTED label; hold-proposal lifts an empty tray only 30px. These four nominal events do not each provide a new meaningful state. A physical site barrier also risks implying actual construction was stopped, which the award-negotiation source does not establish.
notes.fix: Reveal the actual governing status by uncovering a source-backed excerpt and date, then let that evidence change a clearly conceptual proposal layer. Collapse redundant paper handling. Make the empty result space visibly receive no test evidence while a recognizable proposed core stays beside it, or shorten the sequence. Remove any implication that a real site was ordered closed. Reboard the beat list around the genuine evidence changes and preserve a readable hold.

notes.problem: lower-next-test promises a fresh specimen descending into the shaft. The code instead applies -c*330, lifting the fresh rock upward while it remains at x168, far left of the x435 well. The used rock also stays above the same shaft, so an implemented descent could collide unless the old specimen clears it first.
notes.fix: Lift and move the visibly cut specimen onto a separate used tray. Move the visibly different intact specimen over the actual shaft, then lower it in positive y. The same-direction descent should answer the opening image. Retain an explicit proposal cue through this final illustration so the return to action does not read as a completed trial after the no-results scene.

notes.problem: Six visual families and seven picture scenes are declared, but well-cutaway and field-station together occupy 23.9 of 44 story seconds and all scenes share the same hero placement, scale and backdrop planes. This can still feel like framed diagram swaps if the compositor treats the modes uniformly.
notes.fix: Use a true close view for the opening core, a wider surface-to-well relationship for s2, a tactile material macro for s3 and a legible human control close view for s6. Preserve screen direction and core pattern across cuts. The three memorable images should be descending core, bit physically cutting the core with its sensing response, and cut specimen exchanging places with a fresh test specimen.

strongest_frame: s4 around 14.9s, after the bit physically enters the mineral-patterned core. This image can answer why rock is placed underground, provided the damage and the proposed sensing path are large and clear.
weakest_frame: s8 around 38.12s. An empty tray lifts beneath an already readable NOT REPORTED clipboard; the promised new evidence is absent both editorially and physically. It needs a meaningful state change or a shorter hold, not another label.
